strings.name: Taylor Swift
strings.role: Songwriter · Pop music and recording rights
strings.summary: Swift began in Nashville country music before moving into pop, folk and indie styles. Personal storytelling, album concepts and large-scale performances built an international audience. Fearless, 1989, folklore and Midnights each won the Grammy for Album of the Year. Her rerecordings and subsequent purchase of her early masters also brought recording rights and artists’ control into public debate.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected creative, touring and recording-rights milestones cover 1989–October 2026. Award figures refer to stated years, not live totals.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Four Album of the Year awards
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: By 2024, four different albums had won the Grammy for Album of the Year, spanning country, pop and folk styles.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Control of recordings
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: She began releasing Taylor’s Version rerecordings in 2021 and announced the purchase of her first six albums’ masters in 2025.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Large-scale touring
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: The 2023–2024 Eras Tour organized performances around different album periods, connecting her long-running work with international audiences.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Performs at the Academy Museum gala
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Performed at the Los Angeles museum’s annual fundraiser, supporting exhibitions, education and public programs.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Releases The Life of a Showgirl
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Released a new studio album; Spotify reported that it broke the platform’s single-day album streaming record for that year.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Buys back her early masters
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Announced the purchase of the first six albums’ original recordings and related assets from Shamrock Capital, a major resolution of the rights dispute.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Fourth Album of the Year; Eras Tour concludes
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Midnights won the Grammy for Album of the Year. The Eras Tour ended in Vancouver that December.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Begins Taylor’s Version releases
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Released rerecorded versions of Fearless and Red, revisiting early songs and adding previously unreleased material.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Releases folklore
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Moved toward a more pronounced folk and narrative style. The album won Album of the Year at the following Grammys.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Moves further into pop with 1989
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Released a predominantly synth-pop album, expanding her work and audience beyond country music.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Fearless wins Album of the Year
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Her second studio album brought her first Grammy for Album of the Year, marking an early career turning point.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Releases her self-titled debut
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Began her professional career as a teenager in Nashville and wrote or co-wrote every song on the album.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Reading
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Pennsylvania; she later moved to Nashville as a teenager to pursue music.
